headline: Nvidia is building safety technology, called Halos, for robots and self-driving cars so that machines working near people are less likely to hurt them.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: an explainer on a June product with no new event; the sources are Nvidia's own staff.
importance_line: Robots that work beside people in factories and warehouses are being given built-in safety checks rather than fences, which affects workers who share space with them; the claims come from Nvidia and its partners, and no outside test of the system is reported.
summary: Ars Technica reports that Nvidia, the chipmaker, has extended its Halos safety system from self-driving cars to robots in June 2026, combining a safety-focused computer module, monitoring software, simulation and an inspection lab, with Agility Robotics' Digit 5 humanoid the first to build it in. The article relies mainly on Nvidia's own executive, says Nvidia's chief executive put the physical AI business at nearly $10 billion in yearly revenue, and notes that it remains to be seen whether humanoids can become general-purpose workers.
notes: Exact June day of the Halos for Robotics launch is not given, so the freshness date is month-only.
